title: DAIRM: Divyendu's Data-State-Aware AI Reference Model for Generative AI Inference Systems
description:
DAIRM-TR-0001 (Technical Report / Working Draft, version 2.0.0) describes DAIRM, Divyendu's Data-State-Aware AI Reference Model, an informative reference model for the request path of generative AI inference serving.

It defines a six-layer request path (L6 Application, L5 Orchestration & Gateway, L4 Serving Engine, L3 Model Execution Runtime, L2 Device & Driver, L1 Physical Compute & Interconnect) with Context Services, Build/Deploy and Management planes; a named, observable data state at every boundary (request payload, retrieved passages, enriched prompt, token-ID batch and KV-cache block table, kernel launch stream, device instruction and memory-transaction stream, token stream); a boundary-attributed latency diagnostic method that separates context-service delay, serving-engine queueing/KV-cache pressure and memory-bandwidth-bound decode; and a layer-indexed telemetry attribute set (dairm.*).

DAIRM does not claim the layered-stack idea or the OSI analogy as novel; earlier OSI-inspired AI models, including S. Reilly's AOSI reference model (2025), are credited in the report.

This version supersedes AOSI v1.2.1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24073122). The model was renamed DAIRM to avoid confusion with Reilly's earlier AOSI model and restructured after the author's own AI-assisted review (not an external peer review); an unsupported earlier drafting date that appeared in v1.2.1 was removed, and the AI-generated overview image was replaced by source-drawn diagrams. Drafting, editing, formatting and figure preparation were assisted by AI tools; the conceptual model, design decisions and final content are the author's.

Status: Technical Report / Working Draft. IETF Internet-Draft draft-bhatt-dairm-00 prepared, submission pending (not yet submitted; no RFC number; not an IETF standard). arXiv submission pending.

Not an IETF RFC and not a standard. Author: Divyendu Bhatt.
